name: merkle
description: Merkle hash tree over the spec: leaf hashes, interior hashes, snapshots, diff, and impact classification.

requirements.title: Compute leaf hashes
requirements.description: Hash each markdown content file and each JSON file in the spec. Leaf nodes in the merkle tree.

requirements.title: Compute interior hashes
requirements.description: Interior node hashes are computed from the sorted concatenation of their children's hashes. Tree mirrors spec hierarchy: project → module → leaves, with no grouping level between a module and the leaves it declares.

requirements.title: Store snapshots
requirements.description: Write the complete hash tree to the project's snapshot file, committed to git, at the location the lifecycle resolver answers. Loading an absent snapshot is an error, never an implicit empty baseline: the canonical empty tree is no longer Load's forgiving default — it is produced in exactly one place, as the seed value spex init writes — so absence at read time means uninitialised or broken, not 'nothing has changed yet'.

requirements.title: Diff against snapshot
requirements.description: Compare current hash tree against a stored snapshot. Report changed leaves and changed paths (interior nodes whose hash changed).

requirements.title: Classify impact
requirements.description: Classify each change by its impact level: impl_only (only test_section leaves changed), contract (data_flow or api leaves changed — a surface shared beyond one component, either a cross-component shape inside the module or a surface the module declares to its callers), arch_impl (component leaves changed), or structural (module.json or project.json meta leaves changed, or requirement leaves changed). The contract level sits between impl_only and arch_impl: data_flow and api changes are not purely local to a single component, nor do they rewire graph topology like component or meta changes — a data_flow change alters the shapes moving between components and must reach the downstream action classifier so a dedicated data_flow task bead is created. The four levels are fixed; which declared node type maps to which level is read from the resolved profile, the default profile assigns today's types to today's levels unchanged, and a node type the resolved profile does not declare (and that is not meta) is classified unknown — reported on the change's own line in both output formats and in the JSON summary's per-impact counts.

requirements.title: Deterministic hashing
requirements.description: Same file content always produces the same hash. Hash computation is order-independent for interior nodes (children sorted before hashing).

requirements.title: Identity-hash tree keying
requirements.description: Tree nodes are keyed by the spec node's identity hash (the same 12-character hex string stored in the JSON `id` field). The merkle key for a component, requirement, data_flow, test_section, or api is exactly its identity hash — no nested module/type/id path. The keys for synthetic meta leaves use a fixed prefix plus the parent's identity hash (e.g., `meta/<module-hash>` for module.json, `meta/project` for project.json). This makes merkle keys identical to mapping-store `spec_node_id` values, eliminating the rekeying layer that previously translated between the two formats. Renaming a file or moving a directory with the same identity hash is detected as a modification, not a delete + add. The set of node types keyed into the tree, and each type's hashed field allowlist — the policy deciding what counts as a semantic change — are read from the resolved profile; the tree shape itself (project root, module interior nodes, identity-hash-keyed leaves, the synthetic meta leaf per module) is fixed and not declarable.

requirements.title: Change completeness validation
requirements.description: When individual requirement leaf nodes change in the diff (added, modified, or removed), verify that implementing components' content leaves also changed. For modified/added requirements, each implementing component's content leaf must also appear in the diff. For removed requirements, no component may still reference them. For project-level requirement changes, the chain must propagate through module requirements to component leaves. Errors are included alongside changes in the diff JSON output. Which node type triggers the requirement-leaf rules is read from the resolved profile's per-type role flag rather than compiled in — the default profile marks requirement, unchanged; the meta-envelope sweep runs on the fixed meta leaves, a rule of the frame, not a profile assignment.

components.name: Hasher
components.description: Computes SHA-256 hashes for individual files (leaf nodes) and for sorted child hash lists (interior nodes).

components.name: TreeBuilder
components.description: Builds the merkle tree from the parsed spec graph. Each node's key is its spec identity hash (the 12-char hex `id` field) — no path-style keying, no module/type prefix. Requirements are individual leaf nodes with hashes computed from deterministic JSON serialization. Maps spec hierarchy to tree nodes.

components.name: SnapshotStore
components.description: Reads and writes snapshots. Encoding is one operation over bytes: it flattens the identity-hash-keyed tree into the canonical JSON document, and every writer of the snapshot file goes through it, so the format has a single implementation. A plain in-place write over that encoder is offered too, carrying no atomicity; its one production caller is spex init seeding a freshly created state directory — ingest pairs the encoder with its own temp-file-and-rename write. The flat map is keyed by identity hash (hash → {hash, type, ...}), not by file path or integer ID.

components.name: DiffEngine
components.description: Compares two identity-hash-keyed trees (current vs snapshot). Same identity hash + different content hash = modified. Identity hash in current but not snapshot = added. Identity hash in snapshot but not current = removed.

components.name: ImpactClassifier
components.description: Analyzes diff results to classify changes by their impact level. The four levels are fixed; the mapping from declared node type to level is read from the resolved profile handed in as the third input, joined by the fixed meta rule, and the default profile assigns impl_only (test_section), contract (data_flow, api), arch_impl (component) and structural (module.json, project.json, requirement). A node type the profile does not declare is reported as unknown. The contract level is distinct from impl_only because data_flow and api changes describe surfaces shared beyond one component — downstream matchers must not skip them. Uses node metadata (type, module association) instead of parsing path prefixes.

components.name: DiffCommand
components.description: CLI entry point for spex diff. Resolves the profile once per invocation, refusing a malformed one with a single early error before any tree is built. Compares current merkle tree against stored snapshot via DiffEngine, classifies impact via ImpactClassifier, runs change completeness validation via CompletenessChecker — both handed the one resolved profile. Outputs changes and errors in JSON or human-readable format.

components.name: CompletenessChecker
components.description: Validates that requirement leaf changes are accompanied by corresponding component content leaf changes. Reads the current spec graph (project.json, module.json) to resolve requirement-to-component edges via implements arrays. Checks added, modified, and removed requirements for completeness. Also validates component edge changes when meta nodes change without requirement leaf changes.

data_flows.name: Hash computation flow
data_flows.description: Spec files are hashed bottom-up: leaf files → interior nodes → tree root. The tree is then serialized to a snapshot.

data_flows.name: Diff and classification flow
data_flows.description: Current tree and stored snapshot are compared node-by-node. Changed paths are classified by impact level.

apis.name: spex diff
apis.description: Compute changes between snapshot and current spec
